corpusLabel: Demo historical seed — full Key (modern English)
notice: This demo lexicon is drawn from Roger Williams’ 1643 colonial record A Key into the Language of America (public domain). English glosses are modernized for learner clarity. Narragansett spellings are Williams’ ear, not living community orthography. This is a historical scaffold so Keepers and learners can walk a working product. Living Narragansett Knowledge Keepers and speakers hold absolute authority. Production will replace this seed with elder-approved voices and forms.

sourceWork.title: A Key into the Language of America
sourceWork.author: Roger Williams
sourceWork.note: Public domain. Colonial outsider perspective. Learner English modernized. Not living tribal authority.

words.sourceWork: A Key into the Language of America (Roger Williams, 1643)
words.speakerAttribution: Historical record (Williams 1643) — not a living tribal speaker
words.orthographyNote: 17th-century English phonetic spelling of a Narragansett form as heard by Roger Williams (1643). Not a community orthography. Living Narragansett speakers and Knowledge Keepers hold absolute authority.
words.scholarlyNote: Williams recorded Narragansett for English travelers. Multiple forms may appear for one meaning; accent marks attempt stress/length. Historical scaffold only — not a replacement for living speech. Where English is biblical or moralizing, that is Williams’ frame, not tribal doctrine.
